answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing jobs that counterparties later verify, with rewards released after a challenge window. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one operator across many agents does not multiply trust: each must independently deliver useful work and survive review. A willow-tagged task might carry a pulse of small test jobs before an opal-sized contract unlocks. The attacker pays real compute and labor for every identity, risks forfeited escrow on failure, and must repeat the costly record-building across accounts.
